title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law designed to protect AI model creators from theft and unauthorized use. It sets strict penalties for theft, requires companies to implement safeguards, and creates a framework for reporting and prosecuting violations.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent AI companies from exploiting their market power to charge excessively high prices for their services or products. It also seeks to stop AI firms from influencing or manipulating wages, ensuring fair compensation and healthy competition in the labor market.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 creates a framework for studying and monitoring how artificial intelligence is used within the judicial system. It establishes oversight bodies and requires research into AI’s impact on legal proceedings to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 is a federal law that sets out rules and guidelines for how small businesses can develop and use artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to promote responsible AI adoption, protect privacy, and ensure that small businesses benefit from AI innovation while complying with safety and ethical standards.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is aimed at preventing AI systems from misleading people and ensuring users know when they are interacting with AI. It requires companies to clearly label AI-generated content, disclose how the AI works, and give consumers a way to opt out or report deceptive AI practices.

title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act seeks to position the United States as a global AI leader by establishing national standards and promoting collaboration across industry, academia, and government. It aims to create a unified framework that ensures consistent, ethical, and secure AI development and deployment nationwide.

title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks associated with AI systems. It requires federal agencies and private companies to meet new safety standards and reporting obligations, ensuring AI technology is used responsibly and transparently.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: This act aims to encourage the use of artificial intelligence across the financial sector, supporting new technologies and services that can improve efficiency and customer experience. It also establishes guidelines to ensure that AI applications are safe, transparent, and comply with existing financial regulations.

title: HBCU AI Research Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The HBCU AI Research Leadership Act aims to boost AI research and innovation at historically Black colleges and universities. It provides funding, resources, and partnerships to help these institutions become leaders in AI education and development.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to ensure that students from kindergarten through 12th grade understand how artificial intelligence works and how to use it responsibly. It is designed to establish curriculum standards, provide teacher training, and supply schools with the resources needed to teach AI concepts and promote digital literacy.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to stop AI systems from misleading or deceiving people. It requires developers and companies to clearly disclose when content is AI-generated and to give accurate information about the technology so consumers can make informed decisions.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law aimed at regulating the creation, use, and deployment of artificial intelligence models to promote safety and transparency. It focuses on establishing clear testing standards, data governance practices, and oversight mechanisms to address the potential risks and ensure accountability in AI systems.

title: SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Small Business.
summary: The SBA AI Adoption Reporting Act of 2026 is a law that requires the Small Business Administration to track and report how AI technology is being adopted by small businesses across the United States. By collecting this data, the act aims to inform policy decisions, encourage responsible AI deployment, and help small businesses navigate the benefits and risks of AI.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to establish comprehensive rules for the creation, use, and oversight of artificial intelligence systems. It aims to ensure that AI technologies are developed responsibly, with safeguards for safety, fairness, and privacy, while promoting innovation and accountability.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed law that would require companies to evaluate and disclose how their automated systems impact people and society. It aims to increase transparency, reduce bias, and protect consumers by making algorithmic decision‑making more accountable.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 aims to protect individuals from discrimination and bias by ensuring AI systems comply with civil rights laws. It establishes guidelines for transparency, accountability, and oversight of AI applications in public and private sectors to prevent unfair treatment.

title: To prohibit the manufacture and conveyance of certain products for children that incorporate an artificial intelligence chatbot, and for other purposes.
action: Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR H3000-3001)
summary: The policy bans making and selling certain child‑oriented products that use AI chatbots and also covers other related uses. It aims to protect young users from risky or inappropriate AI interactions in these items.

title: To codify Executive Order 14319 (relating to preventing woke AI in the Federal Government).
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: Executive Order 14319 aims to stop federal agencies from using AI that pushes progressive or “woke” viewpoints. This policy will make that order a formal law, requiring federal AI tools to stay neutral and free of political or social bias.

title: To amend the Public Health Service Act to update quality standards for mammography facilities for the use of AI systems, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This legislation amends the Public Health Service Act to revise the quality standards for mammography facilities, specifically to incorporate and regulate the use of AI systems to improve accuracy and patient safety. It also includes additional provisions aimed at supporting broader public health goals and related regulatory updates.

title: American Leadership in AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committees on Energy and Commerce, Agriculture, Oversight and Government Reform, Education and Workforce, the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American Leadership in AI Act is a proposed U.S. law that seeks to keep the United States at the forefront of artificial intelligence by boosting research, development, and responsible deployment. It aims to balance innovation with ethical safeguards and national security interests.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 33 - 0.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2025 establishes a federal initiative to increase research and training in artificial intelligence. It allocates funding and resources to universities, industry, and K‑12 programs to develop AI curricula, support workforce development, and promote equitable access to AI education.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to encourage the export of complete AI systems and components. It seeks to streamline regulations and provide incentives for companies to sell AI technologies overseas, boosting national competitiveness.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is a proposed law designed to shield households from the rising electricity bills that result from the operation of large AI data centers. It aims to achieve this through measures such as regulating energy usage, encouraging renewable power sources, and providing subsidies or incentives to keep utility costs affordable for families.

title: Condemning antisemitism in all its forms, including the proliferation and amplification of antisemitic content on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms, urging robust, transparent safeguards for AI, and recognizing stakeholders working to counter this threat.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy calls for condemning all forms of antisemitism, especially its spread and amplification through AI platforms. It urges the implementation of robust, transparent safeguards and recognizes stakeholders actively working to counter this threat.
